Trump, 20 Feb 2026), briefly replaced by a global 10-15% Section 122 tariff that expired by statute on 24 Jul 2026, and is now superseded by a 10% Section 301 forced-labor tariff -- meaning India's current blanket-tariff rate (10%) ties Bangladesh for the lowest in the peer group compared in this piece, not the highest as originally published. Retitled, rewrote the chart to show current rates instead of the stale Aug 2025 snapshot, rewrote Sections 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6's framing accordingly, added a WTO/GATT Article VI explanation of why AD/CVD survived unaffected while three different blanket-tariff statutes were tried and two were struck down, added Walmart's $2.9bn IEEPA-tariff refund, and updated the caveats/sources cards.

chart bugfix: value-label/category-label collision on two JS-built waterfall charts
version_history.note: This post's charts are built at runtime by inline JS (string-concatenated SVG injected via innerHTML), which tools/svg_chart_lint.py cannot parse (it flags a parse error on the literal '+W+' JS-templating text) -- so this fix was found by rendering the full page in a headless browser (letting the JS execute) and visually inspecting each chart, not by the linter. The shared waterfall() function placed each bar's value label at a fixed offset below the bar's bottom edge; when a bar's bottom coincided with the chart's overall minimum (the exc-cur and exc-fut excise/VAT/exchequer charts, where the VAT and Net-exchequer bars both bottom out at the series minimum), that label collided with the category-name row underneath. Fixed by capping the label's y-position so it can never go below a safe margin above the category-label row, regardless of how close the bar's bottom sits to the plot's edge. Verified by re-rendering all 9 of this post's waterfall/bar charts; the previously-unaffected ones (all-positive bars, which use the top-of-bar label branch) are unchanged.

version_history.note: Publish new post distilling a user-supplied technical brief on SAF/CORSIA pathway certification: corn/maize ethanol-to-jet fails CORSIA's own default carbon-intensity test (90.8-100.6 gCO2e/MJ vs the 89 baseline), worse than the fossil jet fuel it would replace, while MoPNG has been actively promoting maize as an ethanol feedstock since Nov 2023. Also covers molasses having no default value on the ethanol-to-jet route India actually uses (only on the isobutanol route), India's SAF regulatory stack and targets, and the UCO feedstock collection gap. Independently re-verified the core CORSIA CI figures, India SAF target dates, and the IOCL Panipat/Cotecna certification claim via web search rather than taking the source brief on faith. Cross-links the existing isobutanol/ATJ post and the egg-price/maize-ethanol posts.

version_history.note: Amend the CORSIA/corn-ethanol post with recent ICAO/CORSIA data: confirmed ICAO's 8th edition default life-cycle emissions table was approved 19 November 2025 (methodology changes: IPCC 2019 factors, soil-carbon-accumulation credit removed, ATJ-ethanol energy yields refined, new POME HEFA default, broader feedstock coverage); updated Sustainability Certification Scheme approval dates (ISCC/RSB June 2023, ClassNK October 2024, Fourth Edition SCS list June 2026); and added a clarification distinguishing the fuel-eligibility baseline (89 gCO2e/MJ, this piece's subject) from CORSIA's separate sector-wide offsetting baseline (85% of 2019 emissions, 2027-2029 offsetting phase). Confirmed icao.int and a third-party mirror both remain blocked from this research environment on repeated attempts, so the exact revised corn-ethanol/molasses numeric values in the 8th edition could not be pulled directly -- flagged that gap explicitly rather than guessing at the numbers.

version_history.note: Amend the CORSIA/corn-ethanol post using a user-supplied SAF emissions calculator spreadsheet (built around IATA's SAF Accounting and Reporting Methodology, released 31 Jan 2025) and its cited sources. The spreadsheet gives maize a much lower, passing LCA default (43 gCO2e/MJ) than this piece's CORSIA/ISCC figure (90.8-100.6, failing) -- added a section reconciling this rather than silently overwriting either number: explained the IATA formula is a downstream accounting tool for airlines claiming credit on already-purchased SAF, not a CORSIA-eligibility gate, so a calculator populated with an optimistic literature LCA value can compute a real number that still overstates what CORSIA would actually certify. Cited the real academic literature range for corn-ethanol-ATJ (roughly 35-70 gCO2e/MJ across studies) to show the disagreement is real and methodological (ILUC treatment), not an error on either side.
